- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:46:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,

  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2

- **Title**: fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/wire-serve-e4-authn-timeout` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +12

- **Created**: 2026-10-07T01:03:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:46:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

{
  "key": "pr-1358",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)",
    "description": "Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage."

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1358
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1358
- **Title**: fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/wire-serve-e4-authn-timeout` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +12
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T01:03:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:46:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

    test(1337): count any terminal shell-job exit as settled; review follow-ups
    
    Review #1345: settledJobNumbers was hard-pinned to exited(0), so a
    failed job could never satisfy a drain wait built on it — a fully-
    settled stream would poll to the timeout with a misleading missing-
    notices diagnostic. Widen shellJobSettleNotice to exited(-?\d+): any
    exit code is terminal. Lost jobs paint no [bash] notice at all (boot-
    reconcile board count only), documented; lost coverage stays the
    suite's screen-side '. 0 lost' proof. Failing-first unit case: 9x
    exited(0) + 1x exited(127) must satisfy settledJobNumbers==10 (red on
    the old regex, green now).
    
    Also taken from review: waitForRaw( joins the gh-1049 reg guard's
    _windowEnders, and the countdown suite's @Timeout goes 5 -> 8 min so
    the drain's diagnostic-rich TimeoutException outruns the suite ceiling
    in the pathological path (~7 min of stage ceilings).

- **PR #**: 1358
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1358
- **Title**: fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/wire-serve-e4-authn-timeout` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +12
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T01:03:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:46:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

# pr-1358: fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)

## Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

    the old regex, green now).
    
    Also taken from review: waitForRaw( joins the gh-1049 reg guard's

Let me also check one precedent: `85776038d fix(1254): quarantine dracula theme flake + wait headroom for starved shard` — this is a precedent where a flake fix PR included BOTH the quarantine entry AND the wait headroom. And `e75be8726 gh-1014 ... — quarantined, fix + re-enable (#1196)` — fix + re-enable in one PR.

So the repo's convention for a flake-fix PR varies: sometimes the quarantine rides in the same PR (85776038d: "quarantine ... + wait headroom"), sometimes quarantine is a separate lane PR (`flake-quarantine/*` branches: e.g. `flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli`, `flake-quarantine/shell_job_countdown_pty`).

Key point though: the quarantine branch for wire_serve (842fc270d, issue #1360) was authored at 02:05:54Z — AFTER this PR was created (01:03:20Z) and last updated (01:46:05Z). So at authoring time the claim "No fleet-assigned issue exists" was likely true. The quarantine PR is the mechanism that will keep the gate green while the fix lands.

Now, what does this mean for my review?

Finding 1 (IMPORTANT, not blocking): The PR description claims no fleet issue exists, but issue #1360 now exists and covers exactly this E4 flake ("E4 + authn-lite: bad token is rejected; token stays out of records", runs 37552613207 = the exact run cited in the PR!). The PR should link `Closes #1360` (or at least reference it) so the tracker issue closes when this lands, and coordinate the un-quarantine (removing the entry from `flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli`) with this fix landing. Per the quarantine JSON's own comment: "A file listed here is REMOVED from every deterministic Quality-gate integration leg until its fix PR lands". If this fix PR merges and the quarantine entry lands too without removal linkage, the file stays out of the gate indefinitely (well, until un-quarantine proof via nightly). The verdict rules say BLOCKING = "correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss". Is missing linkage a scope violation? It's a process/tracking gap, not a code bug. The code change itself is correct and complete. I'd rate this IMPORTANT — it doesn't break the merge; but it risks the flake's tracker issue never closing and the quarantine coordination being missed.

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me think about whether there's any merge-order hazard: if PR #1358 (the fix) merges BEFORE the quarantine PR (`flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli`) merges, then main gets the fix, and the quarantine PR, when it merges later, would still add the quarantine entry — removing the file from the gate even though it's fixed. That entry would then need un-quarantine. That's the keeper's chore, though. Not this PR's code.

Conversely, the more critical review question for the CODE itself:

Finding 2: The diff is minimal and correct — five 10s→20s bumps, all wire-frame waits now at the file-wide 20s budget. Verified: no `Duration(seconds: 10)` remains. The `connect()` retry loop (200 × 5ms = ~1s max wait, actually up to ~1s of delays plus connection attempts — hmm, interesting: `connect()` tries 200 times with 5ms delay. Under saturation, could the accept loop take longer than ~1s to come up? 200 × 5ms = 1s of pure delay, plus per-attempt overhead. Actually wait — each failed WebSocket.connect attempt throws quickly (connection refused) and then delays 5ms. So the total retry window is roughly 1-2 seconds. Under a saturated runner, `runWireServe` boot could take longer than that... but the PR description says `connect()`'s retry loop was untouched "not the flake mechanism" — the E4 failure was at line 538 (`ws.first.timeout`), i.e., after connect succeeded. OK, that's justified by the evidence: the 401 gate at 527 passed, meaning the server was already up. Fine.

But hold on — is the 200×5ms retry loop actually a latent flake of the same class (one-shot-ish deadline under saturation)? The loop is 200 attempts of `WebSocket.connect` + 5ms delay. Under CPU saturation, 200 attempts each failing fast with connection-refused... the window is ~1s+ of wall time (plus attempt overhead). If boot takes >2s under load, `fail()` fires. But — evidence shows connect succeeded in both failing runs (failure was later at 538). And the PR explicitly scoped it out. I could mention it as a SUGGESTION (the retry loop is a ~1-2s effective budget in a file whose convention is 20s; consider bumping attempts or delay), but the PR's evidence argues the accept loop is up before any connect in the failing path... Actually no — in IT-1/E4, connect happens right after `cli.runWireServe` is called; the server accept loop starts inside the serve closure after boot. The wrong-token 401 gate comes AFTER the first connect in E4? No wait — in E4, the FIRST thing after `runWireServe` is the wrong-token expectLater (line 521-527), then `connect()` at 533. The wrong-token gate passing proves httpListen was live. Then connect() succeeds. So connect's retry budget is not implicated by the evidence. A SUGGESTION at most.

Finding 3: Comment accuracy — the rationale comment says "flake, heads 4a25f2de + 235eeb36". Fine. It references #1311 and #1345. The comment is placed INSIDE the E4 test between the wrong-token gate and the correct-token handshake. It says "The same budget applies to every wire frame wait in this file." OK. One nit: the comment block sits between the wrong-token expectLater and the comment about the right token — there are now two consecutive comment blocks ("// 20s, not 10s:..." then "// The right token works:..."). Readable. Not worth flagging beyond a suggestion? It's fine.

Finding 4: IT-1's three waits (gotFrame/gotSecond/gotReplay) bumped too — matches the stated scope ("all five wire frame round-trip waits"). Good — no scope creep; it's exactly the mechanism class.

Finding 5: Test coverage / no regression test — the PR admits no regression test. For a timing-budget bump in a test file, that's acceptable; the "regression test" is the CI itself. AGENTS.md's flake-lane rule wants quarantine via test_quarantine.json for proven flakes — the quarantine is being handled by the separate `flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli` branch PR. Should THIS PR carry it? Looking at precedent 85776038d "fix(1254): quarantine dracula theme flake + wait headroom for starved shard" — that fix PR bundled quarantine + headroom. But in that case the flake wasn't yet quarantined by another lane. Here, the quarantine lane PR was opened by flake-watch automation AFTER this fix PR was already open. The machine (flake-watch.yml) "files the issue and opens the PR". So the ecosystem is: flake-watch opened #1360 + quarantine PR; this standalone fix PR landed first in time. The right move: link them. I'll flag as IMPORTANT: update the PR description/body to reference issue #1360 (Closes #1360) so the tracker closes on merge, and note the un-quarantine chore for the keeper once this lands (the quarantine entry cites run 37552613207 — the same run evidenced here — so the fix PR and quarantine PR are two views of the same flake).

- **Title**: fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/wire-serve-e4-authn-timeout` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +12
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T01:03:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:46:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

# pr-1358: fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)

## Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

    the old regex, green now).
    
    Also taken from review: waitForRaw( joins the gh-1049 reg guard's

Let me also check one precedent: `85776038d fix(1254): quarantine dracula theme flake + wait headroom for starved shard` — this is a precedent where a flake fix PR included BOTH the quarantine entry AND the wait headroom. And `e75be8726 gh-1014 ... — quarantined, fix + re-enable (#1196)` — fix + re-enable in one PR.

So the repo's convention for a flake-fix PR varies: sometimes the quarantine rides in the same PR (85776038d: "quarantine ... + wait headroom"), sometimes quarantine is a separate lane PR (`flake-quarantine/*` branches: e.g. `flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli`, `flake-quarantine/shell_job_countdown_pty`).

Key point though: the quarantine branch for wire_serve (842fc270d, issue #1360) was authored at 02:05:54Z — AFTER this PR was created (01:03:20Z) and last updated (01:46:05Z). So at authoring time the claim "No fleet-assigned issue exists" was likely true. The quarantine PR is the mechanism that will keep the gate green while the fix lands.

Now, what does this mean for my review?

Finding 1 (IMPORTANT, not blocking): The PR description claims no fleet issue exists, but issue #1360 now exists and covers exactly this E4 flake ("E4 + authn-lite: bad token is rejected; token stays out of records", runs 37552613207 = the exact run cited in the PR!). The PR should link `Closes #1360` (or at least reference it) so the tracker issue closes when this lands, and coordinate the un-quarantine (removing the entry from `flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli`) with this fix landing. Per the quarantine JSON's own comment: "A file listed here is REMOVED from every deterministic Quality-gate integration leg until its fix PR lands". If this fix PR merges and the quarantine entry lands too without removal linkage, the file stays out of the gate indefinitely (well, until un-quarantine proof via nightly). The verdict rules say BLOCKING = "correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss". Is missing linkage a scope violation? It's a process/tracking gap, not a code bug. The code change itself is correct and complete. I'd rate this IMPORTANT — it doesn't break the merge; but it risks the flake's tracker issue never closing and the quarantine coordination being missed.

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me think about whether there's any merge-order hazard: if PR #1358 (the fix) merges BEFORE the quarantine PR (`flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli`) merges, then main gets the fix, and the quarantine PR, when it merges later, would still add the quarantine entry — removing the file from the gate even though it's fixed. That entry would then need un-quarantine. That's the keeper's chore, though. Not this PR's code.

Conversely, the more critical review question for the CODE itself:

Finding 2: The diff is minimal and correct — five 10s→20s bumps, all wire-frame waits now at the file-wide 20s budget. Verified: no `Duration(seconds: 10)` remains. The `connect()` retry loop (200 × 5ms = ~1s max wait, actually up to ~1s of delays plus connection attempts — hmm, interesting: `connect()` tries 200 times with 5ms delay. Under saturation, could the accept loop take longer than ~1s to come up? 200 × 5ms = 1s of pure delay, plus per-attempt overhead. Actually wait — each failed WebSocket.connect attempt throws quickly (connection refused) and then delays 5ms. So the total retry window is roughly 1-2 seconds. Under a saturated runner, `runWireServe` boot could take longer than that... but the PR description says `connect()`'s retry loop was untouched "not the flake mechanism" — the E4 failure was at line 538 (`ws.first.timeout`), i.e., after connect succeeded. OK, that's justified by the evidence: the 401 gate at 527 passed, meaning the server was already up. Fine.

But hold on — is the 200×5ms retry loop actually a latent flake of the same class (one-shot-ish deadline under saturation)? The loop is 200 attempts of `WebSocket.connect` + 5ms delay. Under CPU saturation, 200 attempts each failing fast with connection-refused... the window is ~1s+ of wall time (plus attempt overhead). If boot takes >2s under load, `fail()` fires. But — evidence shows connect succeeded in both failing runs (failure was later at 538). And the PR explicitly scoped it out. I could mention it as a SUGGESTION (the retry loop is a ~1-2s effective budget in a file whose convention is 20s; consider bumping attempts or delay), but the PR's evidence argues the accept loop is up before any connect in the failing path... Actually no — in IT-1/E4, connect happens right after `cli.runWireServe` is called; the server accept loop starts inside the serve closure after boot. The wrong-token 401 gate comes AFTER the first connect in E4? No wait — in E4, the FIRST thing after `runWireServe` is the wrong-token expectLater (line 521-527), then `connect()` at 533. The wrong-token gate passing proves httpListen was live. Then connect() succeeds. So connect's retry budget is not implicated by the evidence. A SUGGESTION at most.

Finding 3: Comment accuracy — the rationale comment says "flake, heads 4a25f2de + 235eeb36". Fine. It references #1311 and #1345. The comment is placed INSIDE the E4 test between the wrong-token gate and the correct-token handshake. It says "The same budget applies to every wire frame wait in this file." OK. One nit: the comment block sits between the wrong-token expectLater and the comment about the right token — there are now two consecutive comment blocks ("// 20s, not 10s:..." then "// The right token works:..."). Readable. Not worth flagging beyond a suggestion? It's fine.

Finding 4: IT-1's three waits (gotFrame/gotSecond/gotReplay) bumped too — matches the stated scope ("all five wire frame round-trip waits"). Good — no scope creep; it's exactly the mechanism class.

Finding 5: Test coverage / no regression test — the PR admits no regression test. For a timing-budget bump in a test file, that's acceptable; the "regression test" is the CI itself. AGENTS.md's flake-lane rule wants quarantine via test_quarantine.json for proven flakes — the quarantine is being handled by the separate `flake-quarantine/wire_serve_cli` branch PR. Should THIS PR carry it? Looking at precedent 85776038d "fix(1254): quarantine dracula theme flake + wait headroom for starved shard" — that fix PR bundled quarantine + headroom. But in that case the flake wasn't yet quarantined by another lane. Here, the quarantine lane PR was opened by flake-watch automation AFTER this fix PR was already open. The machine (flake-watch.yml) "files the issue and opens the PR". So the ecosystem is: flake-watch opened #1360 + quarantine PR; this standalone fix PR landed first in time. The right move: link them. I'll flag as IMPORTANT: update the PR description/body to reference issue #1360 (Closes #1360) so the tracker closes on merge, and note the un-quarantine chore for the keeper once this lands (the quarantine entry cites run 37552613207 — the same run evidenced here — so the fix PR and quarantine PR are two views of the same flake).

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

    test(1337): count any terminal shell-job exit as settled; review follow-ups
    
    Review #1345: settledJobNumbers was hard-pinned to exited(0), so a
    failed job could never satisfy a drain wait built on it — a fully-
    settled stream would poll to the timeout with a misleading missing-
    notices diagnostic. Widen shellJobSettleNotice to exited(-?\d+): any
    exit code is terminal. Lost jobs paint no [bash] notice at all (boot-
    reconcile board count only), documented; lost coverage stays the
    suite's screen-side '. 0 lost' proof. Failing-first unit case: 9x
    exited(0) + 1x exited(127) must satisfy settledJobNumbers==10 (red on
    the old regex, green now).
    
    Also taken from review: waitForRaw( joins the gh-1049 reg guard's
    _windowEnders, and the countdown suite's @Timeout goes 5 -> 8 min so
    the drain's diagnostic-rich TimeoutException outruns the suite ceiling
    in the pathological path (~7 min of stage ceilings).

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1

- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:46:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

# pr-1358: fix(wire-serve): E4 authn flake — wire frame waits get the file-wide 20s budget (2nd distinct-head hit)

## Description

Fixes the 2nd-distinct-head flake: `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` E4 «bad token is rejected; token stays out of records» dying with `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` on PTY shard 2/3 under runner load.

## Evidence — two distinct heads, same signature

| # | Head | CI | Failure |
|---|------|----|---------|
| 1 | `4a25f2de0` (gh-1303/#1305, main run) | PTY shard 2/3 | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538:21` |
| 2 | `235eeb364` (PR #1326 `feat/1321-thin-client-protocol`) | [job 112571629514](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37552613207/job/112571629514) @ 00:36:11Z | E4 `TimeoutException after 0:00:10` @ `:538:21` (115 passed / 2 failed) |

Both hits were on a saturated runner: in run 37552613207 the **co-located countdown leg under-drained in the same shard** (`shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` settled only {1..5} of 10 jobs) — the machine, not the serve, was the constraint.

## Root cause — deadline budget, not a wrong predicate

Drilled job 112571629514 + the harness before touching anything:

- The failing statement (identical on both heads; the file has **zero diff** between `origin/main` and `235eeb364`) is E4's **correct-token** wait: `final first = await ws.first.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))` — the `hello` → `welcome` round-trip.
- The wrong-token 401 gate just before it (line 527) had **passed**, proving `httpListen` was live and the sequential `http.forEach` pipeline was flowing — no transport wedge, no `already_attached` leak, no boot starvation.
- `WireServeServer.attach` → `acceptHello` → `_sendSafely(welcome, send)` is **fully synchronous once the frame lands** — there is no await point and no liveness bug. The only thing that can miss 10s is event-loop scheduling of the round-trip's hops (client add → TCP → decode → attach → welcome → TCP → stream event) under CPU saturation.
- So the failure class is **a one-shot 10s deadline on scheduler-bound I/O with no SLA** — and 10s was an outlier in this very file: every settle/shutdown/error wait already uses the **file-wide 20s budget (#1311's convention)**.

Why not #1345's exact fix shape: the countdown family's disease was a **wrong terminal predicate** (silence-settle could fire mid-drain), so it re-anchored on `waitForRaw` + `shellJobSettleNotice` settled-classification. E4's predicate was already exact — `welcome` is the one legal first server frame, and the kind is asserted after receipt. There is no settle-classification to add; per the flake-lane rule ("if a bump is genuinely the right shape, align to the established convention"), the budget was the only correct knob.

## Fix

`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` only, +12/−5: all **five** wire frame round-trip waits move 10s → 20s — E4's two (the proven failure) **and** IT-1's three (`gotFrame`/`gotSecond`/`gotReplay`, the identical mechanism class rolling the same dice in the same shard). One rationale comment at the E4 site; no new constant (the file inlines `Duration(seconds: 20)` everywhere by convention); `connect()`'s retry loop untouched (not the flake mechanism).

## Verification (disclosure)

- This file is **pure-Dart, PTY-free** (in-process `MemoryExecutionEnv` + loopback `HttpServer`/WebSocket), so the targeted gate ran locally: `dart test test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart --tags integration --concurrency=4` → **9/9 passed** (5.9s), with a temp Dart SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, 3.13.4). The first temp SDK tried (`fah-flutter-sdk`) was SIGKILLed by the host's 137 guard mid-lane — switched SDK once, no retries.
- `dart analyze` on the file: 5 infos, **all pre-existing** (verified against the pristine file — identical set; none on touched lines).
- Honest limitation: no regression test is added — the bug is a real-time deadline vs machine-speed race; a deterministic repro would have to starve the event loop for 10s+ inside CI, which is flake theater. The PR's own CI (pty-integration shards) is the standing regression gate.

No fleet-assigned issue exists for this flake (searched `wire_serve` / E4 / authn-lite; only #1346 countdown + unrelated flakes) — standalone hardening PR, no `Closes` linkage.

    test(1337): count any terminal shell-job exit as settled; review follow-ups
    
    Review #1345: settledJobNumbers was hard-pinned to exited(0), so a
    failed job could never satisfy a drain wait built on it — a fully-
    settled stream would poll to the timeout with a misleading missing-
    notices diagnostic. Widen shellJobSettleNotice to exited(-?\d+): any

    reconcile board count only), documented; lost coverage stays the
    suite's screen-side '. 0 lost' proof. Failing-first unit case: 9x
    exited(0) + 1x exited(127) must satisfy settledJobNumbers==10 (red on
    the old regex, green now).
    
    Also taken from review: waitForRaw( joins the gh-1049 reg guard's
    _windowEnders, and the countdown suite's @Timeout goes 5 -> 8 min so
    the drain's diagnostic-rich TimeoutException outruns the suite ceiling
